camera_bodies.dummy_battery: NP-FW50 dummy battery, e.g. Sony AC-PW20

guidance.text: Use manual (M) or shutter priority. Set the shutter to 1/50 if your mains power is 50 Hz (Europe, most of Asia/Africa/Oceania) or 1/60 if it's 60 Hz (Americas) - this stops light flicker. For 60 fps, use 1/100 (50 Hz) or 1/120 (60 Hz) and add light.
Keep ISO as low as your light allows (under about 1000). If the picture is dark, add light rather than raising ISO.
Set white balance manually (Kelvin or a custom white balance from a white sheet of paper) instead of auto, so colours don't drift.
Use continuous autofocus with face/eye detection, or manual focus on your sitting position.
Use a standard/neutral picture profile, not a log profile.
Don't use the camera's built-in mic - use your real mic in OBS and set an audio sync offset if lips are late.
Menu: Setup > HDMI Settings > HDMI Info. Display: Off, so menus and the focus box don't show on stream.
Set Power Save Start Time to the longest option, and Auto Power OFF Temp to High if your model has it.
Run it on mains power with a dummy battery (NP-FW50 type, e.g. AC-PW20) - a battery won't last a stream and USB power alone often isn't enough.
Check the NTSC/PAL setting: NTSC gives 30/60 fps output, PAL gives 25/50. Match it to your stream frame rate and your mains (PAL + 50 Hz lights avoids flicker).
Flip the screen away from the body and keep the camera ventilated on long streams.

gotchas: Clean HDMI output behaviour, HDMI output resolution/frame rate and auto power-off limits on the a6000 are unverified - check on your camera.
Sony's Imaging Edge Webcam USB support for the a6000 is unverified; use the Cam Link (HDMI) route.
The PC can't change the camera's settings - Setup Coach walks you through the camera menus and checks the result in the image.
